**Retaking a Texas Tech K-12 Course with a Different Teacher**

- Texas Tech K-12 courses are delivered online and teacher assignments are managed by the program.
- If a student (or parent/guardian) wishes to retake a course and requests a different teacher due to previous issues, this request should be communicated directly to Texas Tech K-12.

**How to Request a Different Teacher:**
1. **Submit a Support Request:** Use the [Support Portal](https://www.support.k12.ttu.edu/k12?id=report_issue&sys_id=043a96811b358e50239f0e1de54bcbeb) to explain the situation and request a different teacher for the course retake.
2. **Include Details:** Clearly state the course name, previous teacher, and reason for requesting a different instructor.
3. **Contact Support:** For additional help, you may call Texas Tech K-12 at 1-800-692-6877 or email ttuk12@ttu.edu.

**Important Notes:**
- Teacher assignments are subject to availability and program policies.
- Texas Tech K-12 will review your request and do their best to accommodate, but a specific teacher cannot be guaranteed.

**Next Step:**  
Submit your request through the [Support Portal](https://www.support.k12.ttu.edu/k12?id=report_issue&sys_id=043a96811b358e50239f0e1de54bcbeb) or contact Texas Tech K-12 directly for assistance.

How is taking a single course different from the Full-Time Diploma Program?

To take a single course, students do not need to withdraw from their current school. Students need to obtain approval from their current school Counselor or Principal before enrolling. Students should coordinate with their school Counselor concerning their local school policies and other requirements.

Flexible Curriculum Options

Asynchronous Enrollment:

Students can enroll in courses and Credit by Exams (CBEs) year-round, without enrollment deadlines, making it easy to:

Step 1: Stay on track to graduate on time or early.

Step 2: Recover credits from failed courses.

Step 3: Earn credits during the summer.

Step 4: Access courses not offered at your school.

Step 5: Test out of subjects through Credit By Exams.

Turnkey Full-Time Program for At-Risk Students:

Recommend our online high school diploma program to students struggling in traditional settings. Students transfer to Texas Tech K-12 to complete courses at their own pace, all while being counted as transfers—not dropouts—on district records.

Who should consider an 8-week dual credit course?

Endorsements

Endorsements consist of a related series of courses that provide students with in-depth knowledge of a subject area. Read more information about endorsement choices at the Texas Education Agency Graduation Toolkit (opens in new tab)

Link for "Texas Education Agency Graduation Toolkit (opens in new tab)": https://tea.texas.gov/about-tea/news-and-multimedia/brochures/tea-brochures

Step 1: In addition to the 22 credits earned on the Foundation Plan, college-bound students in Texas Tech High School will complete one advanced course credit in math and science and two credits of targeted electives.

Step 2: Each endorsement option offered by Texas Tech K-12 has one to four required electives to meet the endorsement: Currently, Texas Tech K-12 offers the endorsements in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math, business and industry, arts and humanities, and multidisciplinary studies. Texas Tech K-12 academic advisors will guide you through the endorsement selection process and help you choose an endorsement that best fits your interests and existing credits. You may change your endorsement at any time prior to graduation; however, you should be aware that changes to your endorsement could result in additional required course. See the Personal Graduation Plan Checklist (opens in new tab) for specific courses required for each endorsement.

Link for "Personal Graduation Plan Checklist (opens in new tab)": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/support/pdf/personal-graduation-plan-checklist.pdf

Step 3: All ninth and 10th graders must select an endorsement. After 10th grade, you may opt for the Foundation Plan only with parental consent.

Eligibility and Course Selection

What courses are available in the Full-Time Tuition-Paid Program?

Students have access to a wide range of courses, including:

Step 1: Core subjects (English, math, science, social studies)

Step 2: Electives (art, music, technology, etc.)

Step 3: Foreign languages (Spanish, French, etc.)

Step 4: Advanced Placement (AP) courses

Step 5: Credit recovery and acceleration options

Self-Paced Dual Credit

Choose this option if you want to enroll in an individual, self-paced, dual credit course.

Self-paced courses offer greater flexibility and allow students to progress through their coursework on a more independent schedule.

Apply for Self-Paced Dual Credit (opens in new tab)

Link for "Apply for Self-Paced Dual Credit (opens in new tab)": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/dual-credit/course-info/

ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) USE POLICY (REVISED 2025)

This policy covers any generative Artificial Intelligence tool, such as Chat Generative Pre-trained Transformer, Elicit, Photo Math, etc. This includes text and artwork/graphics/video/audio, etc.

All work submitted in this course must be your own. You may not use artificial intelligence tools to complete your assignments in this course.

If an instructor suspects that an assignment is not the work of the student, it will receive a score of zero. The instructor will message the student or provide feedback on the assignment indicating the need to schedule a one-on-one video conference, during which the student will be required to demonstrate their skills or knowledge through an alternative or mutually agreed-upon assignment. The grade of the alternate or agreed upon assignment will be determined at the instructor’s discretion with the highest possible score being 70%.

If it is determined that a student has violated final exam directions on Final Exam A or Credit By Exam Set 1, the exam will be scored as zero. The student may take Final Exam B or Credit By Exam Set 2 with the highest possible score being 70%.

The incident will be reported to Texas Tech K-12 Administration and documented in the student’s file. Continued violations of Texas Tech University’s Academic Integrity Policy will result in the removal of the student from the program. Texas Tech Student Handbook (opens in new tab)

Link for "Texas Tech Student Handbook (opens in new tab)": https://www.depts.ttu.edu/dos/Studenthandbook2022forward/StudentHandbook2022-2023.pdf

Becoming a Texas Tech K-12 student is easy and offers numerous benefits: graduate on time or early, make up failed credits, take courses not offered in your school, earn credits during the summer without attending traditional summer school, supplement your school or homeschool curriculum, and work at a pace that's right for you. Eligibility and Course Selection

Final Grade Point Calculation for Graduation

Texas Tech K-12 uses the guidelines below to compute your final Grade Point Average (GPA) in Texas Tech High School:

Step 1: Texas Tech K-12 computes the GPA for graduation using all accredited Texas Tech K-12 courses that apply to graduation

Step 2: Each numerical grade will be assigned the following points:

Grade to Points Conversion | Grade to Points Conversion | Grade to Points Conversion | Grade to Points Conversion

------------------------------------------------------------

Numerical Grade | Alphabetic Grade | Points for Regular Courses | Points for Honors, Advanced Placement, and Dual-Credit Courses

90-100 | A | 4.0 | 5.0

80-89 | B | 3.0 | 4.0

75-79 | C | 2.0 | 3.0

70-74 | D | 1.0 | 2.0

0-69 | F | 0.0 | 0.0

All course grades while you are enrolled in Texas Tech K-12 will be recorded on your transcript and used in computing your final Grade Point Average. However, you may replace a failing grade you received on a Texas Tech K-12 course or Credit By Exam by repeating the course or Credit By Exam.

Transfer Grades for the High School Program

All grades transferred to Texas Tech High School from another accredited school will be used in computing your final GPA except for local credit courses and courses scored on a pass/fail scale.

Grades on homeschool transcripts and transcripts from non-accredited schools are not transferable. To receive credit for non-accredited courses, you must take Credit by Exams (CBEs) or enroll in the courses.

If you have failed a previous transfer course, you may repeat the course for credit with Texas Tech High School.

The following designations will receive weighted credits:

Step 1: Advanced Placement (AP) or Passing (P)

Step 2: Honors

Step 3: International Baccalaureate (IB)

- Art
- Music Appreciation
- Health
- Physical Education
- Career Exploration
- Personal Financial Literacy
- Technology Applications
- Communication Applications (Speech)
- Psychology
- Sociology

- Visit the [Texas Tech K-12 Course Catalog](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/support/coursedescriptions.php) for a full list of elective offerings and course descriptions.
- Before enrolling, check with your school counselor to ensure the elective will count toward your graduation requirements.

**Next Step:**
- Review the [course catalog](https://www.depts.ttu.edu/k12/support/coursedescriptions.php) and select the elective(s) that best fit your interests and graduation plan.
